goal: Diagnose why our largest customer's onboarding takes too long and ship a fix, ending with an approved response back to the customer.

acceptance: Names the account, contract value, renewal date, and who raised the complaint
Lists each onboarding milestone with its actual date and the days spent in it
Quotes the customer's own words about what felt slow, with source
Documents every onboarding step end to end with the owning team and handoff point
Marks each step's target duration versus the observed duration for this account
Flags every step with no named owner or no defined SLA
Reports median and p90 time-to-value across all customers, not just this one
Ranks onboarding steps by total delay contributed, with the numbers shown
States sample size and any data gaps that weaken the ranking
Separates delays caused by the product from delays caused by people or process
Names the top three product friction points with evidence from step data
States which friction points block go-live versus merely annoy
Confirms or rejects each product friction point against the actual system behavior
Gives a rough build size (small/medium/large) for fixing each confirmed blocker
Lists any blocker that is a config or data issue rather than a code issue
Lists every security, questionnaire, or access-review gate inside onboarding with its typical duration
States which gates are genuinely required and which are habit
Proposes a faster path for required gates without weakening the control
Lists contract, DPA, and signature steps in onboarding with observed turnaround times
Identifies clauses or redline loops that repeatedly stall onboarding
States any legal step that cannot be shortened and why
States the top three root causes ranked by days of delay they explain
Traces each root cause to named evidence from an earlier step
Explicitly says what was ruled out and why
Every root cause has at least one fix with a named owning department
Each fix has a target date and a measurable before/after number
Separates quick fixes shippable this month from longer builds
Gives the new step-by-step onboarding flow with one named owner per step
Sets an SLA in days for every step and a total time-to-value target
Shows what changed versus the old flow in a short before/after list
Defines time-to-value and per-step duration metrics with exact calculation rules
Sets a baseline number and a target number for each metric
Names where each metric is measured and how often it is refreshed
Confirms each engineering fix is buildable within its stated target date
Flags any fix that depends on work not yet scoped or staffed
Gives a clear go/no-go per engineering item
Estimates cost and headcount time for the plan against the account's revenue at risk
States whether any item needs new spend approval and how much
Gives a plain recommendation on whether the plan is worth funding
Names what we found, what we are changing, and by when, in plain language
Makes no commitment that the validated plan does not already support
Includes a concrete next check-in date with the customer
Lists every item needing a human yes: spend, customer message, process change
States the recommendation and the risk of doing nothing for each item
Fits on one page a busy executive can decide from
